still_wrong.from: new, caused by the speed-3 fix (round 2 blocker 1 comes back in the usual flow)
still_wrong.title: Opening the deformation shows torn, holed walls for the whole play, every loop, until it is paused (default and Max mesh, principal surface)
still_wrong.detail: Opening the deformation starts the play at t = 0 at once (app.js openTransport). The speed-3 fix never draws a chain program for the first time in a moving frame. edgeAhead first-draws the deformation's edge pass only at rest, once it has settled (900 ms after its link). So when the user opens the deformation, no rest frame comes, and every play frame uses the former 0.3 H rule (cuts -1). The walls next to the cut get jagged teeth and holes, the same picture as the base. Round 2 draws them clean. With Loop on it stays torn on the second and third pass (frames at 3 s and 6 s, t = 0.001 and 0.099). The same build is clean if the transport is opened and the play starts 1.2 s or 2.5 s later. All sheets is clean (a different path). The review's and the builder's real-play gates missed it because they set a rest t first, which warms the edge pass. Desktop 1440x900 light, sin sqrt z, Im, default mesh and Max.
still_wrong.evidence: notes/landscape-walls/r3/review-verify/open-and-play-torn-walls-loop.png (row 1: this build, open and play at once, frames at 0.4, 3.0 and 6.0 s, then round 2 at 6 s, clean; row 2: this build with a 1.2 s wait, clean, then the base, torn; row 3: a 2.5 s wait, clean, then round 2 at 3 s); open-and-play-default-mesh-r3-all-base-r2.png (rows: this build principal t ~0.04-0.7 torn; this build All sheets clean; base torn; round 2 clean); open-and-play-max-mesh.png (Max, t 0.002-0.47, torn). Raw: work/xvls/test/rv3v_cdp/shots/Q-*, Q2-*; qp2.out.json, quickplay.out.json; cmd/quickplay_body.js, cmd/qp2_body.js.
still_wrong.fix: Let the edge pass be ready before the first play frame: start compiling it with the chain whenever a deformation can open (or when the step card shows its play control), and first-draw it with a write-nothing pass at the last rest frame. If it is still cold when the play starts, take the one first-draw stall at t = 0 rather than tear the whole play, or draw with round 2's moving path until it is ready. Add an 'open and play at once, Loop on' case to the motion gate, default and Max meshes, light and dark.

still_wrong.from: new (not in the base; seen only in this build)
still_wrong.title: WebGL errors every frame while a two-step deformation plays with All sheets: texImage2D 'ArrayBufferView not big enough' and texSubImage2D 'Offset overflows texture dimensions'
still_wrong.detail: A fresh custom formula with a square root after sqrt z (sin sqrt(z^2 + c)), All sheets on, Landscape opened, then the deformation over f1 -> f2 played 1 s later. In 3 of 3 runs that logged per page, this build logged WebGL errors while it played: 94 in 6.5 s in 2 runs, 50 in 1.5 s in a third. First one INVALID_OPERATION texImage2D 'ArrayBufferView not big enough for request', then GL_INVALID_VALUE glTexSubImage2DRobustANGLE 'Offset overflows texture dimensions' every frame. They begin when the play loops from t = 2 back into the first step (the third run: 0 errors up to t = 2 at 5.5 s, 50 by t = 0.96 at 7 s). None after it stops. The base logged none in 3 of 3. Round 2 logged 1 message in the same flow (not inspected). The user's own case (one-step range) logged none. Likely cause (not proven): rfApply writes the level and list textures in place when o.lvDim / o.lstRows match ('written in place, r3'). After a failed or mis-sized texImage2D the size fields still claim the old size, so every later texSubImage2D fails and the refinement reads levels that do not match the heights. The picture breaks with them: in the errored frame (t = 0.96) a straight white slit runs across both sheets, from the block's edge to the branch point, with a loose sliver beside it. The same frame of the base and this build at rest after the stop have none.
still_wrong.evidence: notes/landscape-walls/r3/review-verify/warn.out.json (per page and phase), cardplay.out.json (first sighting). allsheets-two-step-errors-slit-t0.96.png (left: playing with the errors, t = 0.964; right: after the stop); allsheets-two-step-errors-r3-vs-base.png (top: this build at t = 0.79, 0.96 and stopped; bottom: base at the same moments); warn2.out.json (t and error count per frame). Command: cmd/warn_body.js, cmd/cardplay_body.js.
still_wrong.fix: Find the texture: log the size of each texImage2D/texSubImage2D against its data in rfApply, rfBuild and runTFRows for this case. Set lvDim/lstRows only after a successful allocation, and check the data length (Mq x M x 4, 1024 x rows) before writing in place. Make 'no WebGL errors or warnings' a check in landscape_walls_cmd.js, with a two-step deformation and All sheets.

still_wrong.from: speed-5 fix (3 s cap) together with speed-2
still_wrong.title: A fresh formula with All sheets, deformation started soon after the open: 305 to 724 ms freezes during the play in 2 of 5 runs (base: none over 113 ms in 5)
still_wrong.detail: sin sqrt(z^2 + c) after sqrt z, All sheets, Landscape opened, deformation f1 -> f2 played 1 s later, frame gaps over the next 8 s. This build: 710 ms at 1.1 s and 724 ms at 2.96 s (run 1), 305 ms at 1.67 s (run 2), none over 100 in the other three runs (cardplay and warn). Base: largest gap after the play started 113 ms, in 5 runs. The 2.96 s freeze matches the card wait's new 3 s cap: the step cards' Landscape programs then compile and are first drawn while the pane plays. The 1.1 s one is the play's own first frames. Mid-play freezes are what the user sees as a stuck animation.
still_wrong.fix: Never let the cap release a card's first draws into a moving frame. Release it at the next rest frame, or warm the card programs with a write-nothing draw at the pane's rest frames. Measure mid-play gaps with fresh formulas, base alternating.
